title: Review: Stress–strain and force–extension behaviour; Elastic strain energy; Progressive waves; Stationary waves and harmonics
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; MT02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; W01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; W01-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MT03-1#N.4, W01-1#N.15, W01-uk1#N.3, W10-1#N.4a, MT03-1#N.8, W01-1#N.1, W01-uk1#N.10, W10-1#N.10, MT03-1#N.11, W01-uk1#N.5. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Longitudinal wave
items.clue: Has oscillations parallel to the direction of energy transfer, as in sound.

items.label: Limit of proportionality
items.clue: Point on a force–extension graph beyond which the line is no longer straight.

items.label: Wavelength
items.clue: Distance between the nearest points that move in step, such as crest to crest.

items.label: Transverse wave
items.clue: Has oscillations perpendicular to the direction in which energy travels, as on a string.

questions.stem: A steel wire obeys Hooke's law. A tension of 60 N gives an extension of 1.2 mm. How much elastic strain energy does the wire store?
questions.explanation: Energy = ½ × force × extension = ½ × 60 × 1.2 × 10⁻³ = 0.036 J.

questions.stem: A vibrator sends waves along a stretched string at constant tension. At 25 Hz the wavelength is 0.80 m. The frequency is raised to 100 Hz. What is the new wavelength, and how long does a wave now take to travel 4.0 m along the string?
questions.explanation: v = fλ = 25 × 0.80 = 20 m s⁻¹, unchanged. New λ = 20/100 = 0.20 m; time = 4.0/20 = 0.20 s, the same as before.

questions.stem: Two points on a progressive wave of wavelength 1.2 m are 0.40 m apart along the direction of travel. What is the phase difference between their oscillations?
questions.explanation: Right. Δx/λ = 0.40/1.2 = ⅓ cycle, and ⅓ × 2π = 2π/3 rad (120°).

questions.stem: A string fixed at both ends vibrates in a standing wave. Its nodes are at x = 0, 0.40 m, 0.80 m and 1.20 m, measured from one end. Points P, Q and R on the string are at x = 0.10 m, 0.20 m and 0.70 m. Which statement about the oscillations of P, Q and R is correct?

options.text: P and Q oscillate π/4 rad out of phase, being λ/8 apart.
P and Q oscillate in phase, with amplitudes equal to each other.
P and R oscillate in antiphase, with equal amplitudes.
P and R oscillate in phase, with equal amplitudes.

questions.stem: The spring in a toy dart launcher has a spring constant of 400 N m⁻¹. It is compressed by 0.030 m and then released, firing a dart of mass 0.012 kg horizontally. All the elastic potential energy is transferred to the dart's kinetic energy. What is the speed of the dart?
A loudspeaker plays a steady note to a listener 5 m away in a room with still air. Which of the following travels from the loudspeaker to the listener?

options.text: Energy, passed along by air molecules that vibrate about fixed positions
Air molecules, pushed across the room from the loudspeaker to the ear
Sound particles, which the loudspeaker gives off and the air carries
An electromagnetic signal, which needs no air to carry it across

questions.stem: A loudspeaker emits a steady 500 Hz note. Two microphones are placed on a straight line from the loudspeaker, 0.17 m apart. The speed of sound is 340 m s⁻¹. How do the oscillations detected by the two microphones compare?

options.text: They are in antiphase, π rad apart.
They are a quarter of a cycle, π/2 rad, apart.
They are in phase, as the note has one frequency.
They are an eighth of a cycle, π/4 rad, apart.

questions.stem: A string fixed at both ends vibrates in its first harmonic. The tension in the string is then increased to four times its original value, with the length and the string unchanged. By what factor does the frequency of the first harmonic change?
A spring obeys Hooke's law. When it is compressed by 3.0 cm it stores 0.45 J. How much energy does it store when it is compressed by 4.5 cm?
questions.explanation: Energy ∝ (compression)². The compression is 1.5 times larger, so E = 0.45 × 1.5² = 1.0 J.

questions.stem: Two displacement–time graphs, P and Q, show the oscillations of two points on a wave. Both have a period of 6.0 ms. Each crest of Q comes 1.0 ms after the matching crest of P. What is the phase difference between P and Q?
